text:
maria: Quick note

I'm seeing reproducible token drift after we enable the new rope-rescale path during a live quantized reshard. Triggered only on >48k contexts, 4-shard configs. Single-shard and cold-start int4 runs are clean.

owen: interesting. Does the drift correlate with the rescale call or with any GC/flush activity?

maria: aligns with the rescale call + kv remap that runs as part of the hot-resume. The stream runs for ~50k tokens, we call rescale at ~49.2k and then observe one-to-two wrong tokens inserted then stream realigns.

jin: can you paste a compact token diff? small snippets make it easier to reason about aliasing.

maria: sure (global_pos included):
```
pos: 49185 49186 49187 49188 49189 49190 49191
expected: ... 44 9 77 320 18 2 401
actual:   ... 44 9 77 320 18 999 2 401
# single unexpected token (999) at pos 49190 then recovery
```

owen: single unexpected token then recovery -> smells like a transient write landed to the wrong local_index slot on one shard while others were reading. If remap is not atomic across shards you can get a write into an old mapping that later gets overwritten.

maria: I attached the per-shard kv index dump right before and after rescale. After rescale, shard 3 shows local_stride=32 but local_pos_base didn't update (still old base). Others updated.

jin: did we change stride semantics in the rescale patch? I recall we made stride adaptive based on sequence length distribution (commit 9f2ba8). That could affect index remap math if some shards assume old stride when computing local_index.

maria: repro command used: 
```
./serve --model stella40b --shards 4 --context 131072 --quant int4 --streaming --rescale-on-highctx
# trigger: POST /admin/rescale?mode=adaptive
```

owen: can you post a trimmed kv dump (global_pos -> shard, local_index) for region 49160-49200? nice to see collisions.

maria: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# before rescale (global_pos -> shard:local_index)
49188 -> 1:120
49189 -> 2:121
49190 -> 3:122
49191 -> 0:123
# after rescale
49188 -> 1:120
49189 -> 2:121
49190 -> 3:58  # unexpected remap
49191 -> 0:123
```

jin: yep, 49190 remapped to a small index on shard 3 causing the write to collide with earlier data. That explains the transient token substitution. Strange that remap produced an index already in use; remap should compute non-overlapping ranges based on pos_base and stride.

owen: two likely root causes: (A) stride change happened on some shards but not others because rescale updates stride asynchronously, or (B) pos_base commit races with remap calculation. Either way we need stronger ordering.

maria: local quick mitigation: disable adaptive rescale on longsession runs (flag off in canary config). 

jin: longer term fix: make remap+pos_base+stride changes atomic across shards (barrier) and add a validation pass after remap that checks for overlapping local_index ranges for the affected global_pos window. If overlap found, abort and roll back.

ops-bot: CI flake detected: eng-ml/longctx-rescale-smoke #8901 failed on canary - logging: https://redwood.internal/ci/8901

nowen: also add an integration test that fires adaptive rescale mid-stream on randomized prompts (diverse tokens) and asserts no ghost insertions for 100k tokens. Synthetic repeats won't catch index aliasing.

jin: I'll own a small unit that simulates remap with staggered shard updates and asserts that computed local_indices are monotonic and disjoint for a test window. That should have caught this in pre-commit if present.

maria: thanks. I'll file an incident summary with dumps and the small reproducer (curl + prompt) and assign to jin/owen. Priority P1 for dedicated longsession customers.

owen: PR plan: revert the adaptive stride change in rescale (temporary), add atomic commit for pos_base/stride, and add two tests: (1) remap-barrier integration, (2) longstream-rescale regression. I'll open the revert PR early to stop customer hits.
